concept_blocks.I: MCP or equivalent tool-integration protocol (function calling, tool schema)
concept_blocks.D: GIS / geospatial domain (QGIS, ArcGIS, PostGIS, spatial analysis)
concept_blocks.C: construct per RQ: effectiveness, difficulty/determinism, tool count, security, fidelity

meta.note: One AND per query was the old rule; the revision keeps one AND per *concept block* and allows OR inside a block, which is what arXiv/PQ boolean syntax actually supports.

queries.concept: MCP x GIS (existence / core gap query)
queries.scopus: TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "model context protocol" OR "mcp server*" OR "mcp tool*" OR "mcp-based" ) AND TITLE-ABS-KEY ( gis OR "geographic information system*" OR geospatial OR geoprocessing OR qgis OR arcgis OR postgis OR "spatial analysis" OR "spatial reasoning" OR "spatial data" ) AND PUBYEAR > 2023 AND PUBYEAR < 2027 AND LANGUAGE ( english ) AND DOCTYPE ( ar OR cp OR re )
queries.arxiv: (abs:"Model Context Protocol" OR abs:"MCP server" OR abs:"MCP servers" OR abs:"MCP tool") AND (abs:GIS OR abs:geospatial OR abs:"geographic information" OR abs:QGIS OR abs:"spatial analysis" OR abs:geoprocessing OR abs:PostGIS)

openalex.filter: title_and_abstract.search:"model context protocol"|"mcp server"|"mcp servers"|"mcp tool",title_and_abstract.search:gis|geospatial|qgis|postgis|"geographic information"|"spatial analysis",publication_year:>2023

queries.why: Bare acronym 'MCP' was in S1/A1; in Scopus it collides with membrane cofactor protein, monocyte chemoattractant protein, metacarpophalangeal, multi-chip package. Spell the protocol out and add the MCP-prefixed noun phrases.

queries.concept: bare-acronym recall guard (papers that only ever write 'MCP')
queries.scopus: TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "MCP" ) AND TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "large language model*" OR LLM* OR "ai agent*" OR agentic ) AND TITLE-ABS-KEY ( gis OR geospatial OR qgis OR arcgis OR postgis OR "spatial analysis" ) AND PUBYEAR > 2023 AND NOT TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "membrane cofactor protein" OR "monocyte chemoattractant protein" OR metacarpophalangeal OR "multi-chip package" OR "magnetic cloud plasma" )
queries.arxiv: abs:MCP AND (abs:"large language model" OR abs:LLM OR abs:agent OR abs:agentic) AND (abs:GIS OR abs:geospatial OR abs:QGIS)
queries.why: The NOT block is the price of searching bare 'MCP'; without it you drown in biomedical hits.

queries.concept: MCP vs CodeGen / function calling (the head-to-head the thesis claims is missing)
queries.scopus: TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "model context protocol" OR "mcp server*" OR "mcp tool*" OR "mcp-based" ) AND TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "code generation" OR "function calling" OR "tool calling" OR "tool use" OR pyqgis OR "code interpreter" OR "python code" ) AND PUBYEAR > 2023 AND PUBYEAR < 2027 AND LANGUAGE ( english )
queries.arxiv: (abs:"Model Context Protocol" OR abs:"MCP server") AND (abs:"code generation" OR abs:"function calling" OR abs:"tool calling" OR abs:PyQGIS)

openalex.filter: title_and_abstract.search:"model context protocol"|"mcp server",title_and_abstract.search:"code generation"|"function calling"|"tool calling"|pyqgis,publication_year:>2023

queries.why: This is the query whose result set decides the novelty claim. If it returns a controlled MCP-vs-CodeGen GIS study, the gap closes.

queries.scopus: TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "model context protocol" OR "mcp server*" OR "mcp-based" ) AND TITLE-ABS-KEY ( benchmark* OR evaluat* OR assessment* OR "empirical study" OR "comparative study" OR replication ) AND PUBYEAR > 2023 AND PUBYEAR < 2027 AND LANGUAGE ( english ) AND DOCTYPE ( ar OR cp OR re )
queries.arxiv: (abs:"Model Context Protocol" OR abs:"MCP server") AND (abs:benchmark OR abs:evaluation OR abs:"empirical study" OR abs:"comparative study")
queries.why: Kept close to old S3 but without the domain block, which belonged in a separate query (Q7) — mixing them made S3 answer two questions at once.

queries.scopus: TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "model context protocol" OR "mcp server*" OR "mcp tool*" ) AND TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "tool poisoning" OR "prompt injection" OR "attack surface" OR "capability exposure" OR "least privilege" OR "confused deputy" OR "malicious server" OR "supply chain attack" OR "rug pull" OR secur* OR attack* ) AND PUBYEAR > 2023 AND PUBYEAR < 2027 AND LANGUAGE ( english )
queries.arxiv: (abs:"Model Context Protocol" OR abs:"MCP server") AND (abs:security OR abs:attack OR abs:"prompt injection" OR abs:"tool poisoning" OR abs:"least privilege" OR abs:"attack surface")

openalex.filter: title_and_abstract.search:"model context protocol"|"mcp server",title_and_abstract.search:security|attack|"prompt injection"|"tool poisoning"|"attack surface",publication_year:>2023

queries.why: Added the four Hou-et-al. threat classes that A5's OR-chain was reaching for, plus parenthesisation — the old A5 chain produced 75,099 hits because the OR bound looser than the AND.

queries.concept: tool-set size / tool retrieval / schema overhead
queries.scopus: TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "tool retrieval" OR "tool discovery" OR "tool selection" OR "tool search" OR "tool recommendation" OR "tool overload" OR "tool library" OR "toolset size" OR "number of tools" OR "tool description*" ) AND TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "large language model*" OR LLM* OR agent* OR agentic ) AND PUBYEAR > 2023 AND PUBYEAR < 2027 AND LANGUAGE ( english )
queries.arxiv: (abs:"tool retrieval" OR abs:"tool selection" OR abs:"tool discovery" OR abs:"tool search" OR abs:"tool overload" OR abs:"tool count") AND (abs:"language model" OR abs:LLM OR abs:agent OR abs:agentic)

openalex.filter: title_and_abstract.search:"tool retrieval"|"tool selection"|"tool discovery"|"tool overload"|"tool description",title_and_abstract.search:"large language model"|llm|agentic,publication_year:>2023

queries.why: PB7 is about tool *count*, so 'toolset size', 'number of tools', 'tool description' and 'tool overload' had to enter the vocabulary; the old S5 stopped at retrieval synonyms and forced a GIS term, which suppressed the general MCP tool-count literature the thesis needs for H7a-e.

queries.concept: determinism / reproducibility of agentic tool use
queries.scopus: TITLE-ABS-KEY ( agent* OR "large language model*" OR LLM* ) AND TITLE-ABS-KEY ( determinis* OR reproducib* OR "run-to-run" OR "non-determinism" OR "variance across runs" ) AND TITLE-ABS-KEY ( tool OR "function calling" OR "tool calling" OR "code generation" OR workflow ) AND PUBYEAR > 2022 AND PUBYEAR < 2027 AND LANGUAGE ( english )
queries.arxiv: (abs:determinism OR abs:deterministic OR abs:"non-determinism" OR abs:"run-to-run") AND (abs:"language model" OR abs:"language models" OR abs:LLM) AND (abs:tool OR abs:"function calling" OR abs:"tool calling")
queries.why: Missing entirely from the old protocol, yet ED (execution determinism) is a primary metric and PB6 is a fidelity claim. Without this query the ED discussion has no citable baseline. Tightened 2026-10-31: the first formulation returned 2,352 arXiv / 43,529 OpenAlex hits (determinism × agent is a control-theory topic); requiring an LLM phrase plus a tool term brings it to a screenable size.

queries.concept: cross-domain MCP evaluation (medical / legal / scientific) — the 'other domains did this, GIS did not' argument
queries.scopus: TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "model context protocol" OR "mcp server*" ) AND TITLE-ABS-KEY ( medical OR clinical OR healthcare OR legal OR law OR finance OR "scientific computing" OR chemistry OR bioinformatics ) AND TITLE-ABS-KEY ( benchmark* OR evaluat* OR assessment* OR case study ) AND PUBYEAR > 2023 AND PUBYEAR < 2027 AND LANGUAGE ( english )
queries.arxiv: (abs:"Model Context Protocol" OR abs:"MCP server") AND (abs:medical OR abs:clinical OR abs:legal OR abs:finance OR abs:scientific OR abs:bioinformatics) AND (abs:benchmark OR abs:evaluation OR abs:"case study")
queries.why: Separated from Q3 so that the 'domain coverage' table in Ch. III.4 can be built from one query instead of being a by-product.

queries.scopus: TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "MCP-Bench" OR "LiveMCPBench" OR "MCP-Universe" OR "MCPToolBench" OR "MCP-Atlas" OR "GeoAnalystBench" OR "GeoAgentBench" OR "GeoNatureAgent" OR "GeoJSON Agents" OR "GIS Copilot" OR "OGSAgent" OR "GISclaw" OR "MCPacific" OR "LLM-Geo" ) AND PUBYEAR > 2022
queries.arxiv: all:"MCP-Bench" OR all:"LiveMCPBench" OR all:"MCP-Universe" OR all:"MCPToolBench" OR all:"MCP-Atlas" OR all:"GeoAnalystBench" OR all:"GeoAgentBench" OR all:"GeoNatureAgent" OR all:"OGSAgent" OR all:"GIS Copilot" OR all:"LLM-Geo" OR all:"MCPacific"
queries.why: The old recall test was a checklist applied after the fact. Making the known items a query turns recall into a measurement and pulls in papers that cite/derive from them.

queries.concept: domain-anchored paradigm comparison, protocol-agnostic (catches precedents that never say 'MCP')
queries.scopus: TITLE-ABS-KEY ( gis OR geospatial OR qgis OR arcgis OR postgis OR "geographic information system*" OR "spatial analysis" ) AND TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "function calling" OR "tool calling" OR "tool use" OR "code generation" OR "tool-augmented" ) AND TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "large language model*" OR LLM* OR agent* ) AND PUBYEAR > 2022 AND PUBYEAR < 2027 AND LANGUAGE ( english )
queries.arxiv: (abs:GIS OR abs:geospatial OR abs:QGIS OR abs:"geographic information" OR abs:"spatial analysis") AND (abs:"function calling" OR abs:"tool calling" OR abs:"tool use" OR abs:"code generation" OR abs:"tool-augmented")
queries.why: ADDED after the first automated run: GeoJSON Agents (2509.08863) — the closest precedent in the KB — was MISSING from every MCP-anchored query because the paper never names MCP. The novelty claim therefore cannot rest on an intervention-anchored query alone: recall must be measured on the domain-anchored query, with the MCP block used only to differentiate.

known_items_recall_test.rule: If a known item is absent from every automated query, add its title terms to the vocabulary of the failing block — do not add it to the results by hand.

snowballing.method: forward + backward citation chase, 1 hop, via OpenAlex cited_by / referenced_works; stop when new relevant hits = 0 for 50 records
snowballing.why: OGSAgent (IJGIS, Aug 2026) is invisible to arXiv-only search and thin in Scopus abstracts; citation chasing is how the KB actually found it.
